item.title: China, U.S. youth seek connection, cooperation via exchange program
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- For 16-year-old Otoota Uipi, who has studied Chinese for more than a decade and counts Chinese pop star Jay Chou among her favorite artists, visiting China for the first time fulfilled a long-held dream. Already familiar with the Chinese language and pop culture, the U.S. teenager was still struck by technological innovations: hotel service robots, advanced university labs, and digital tools woven into ordinary life. Gathering roughly 200 students from China and the United States, the Beijing trip earlier this week came amid a major expansion of bilateral people-to-people ties. In November 2023, China announced a five-year initiative to invite 50,000 young Americans to China for exchange and study programs. The target was met two and a half years ahead of schedule earlier this year. It recently launched a new plan to invite 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchange and study over the next five years. The three-day event, co-hosted by the China Education Association for International Exchange and Peking University and designed to help young people move beyond stereotypes and connect directly across cultures, featured campus tours, cultural activities and roundtable talks. Uipi explored university campuses with her Chinese peers, swapping stories about local food and everyday tech use. She called these conversations "an interesting experience." Maria Sablan, a college student from Saipan in the U.S. Northern Mariana Islands, gained a new perspective on China. Accustomed to life in a quieter island community, she had worried China's bustling cities would overwhelm her. Those fears faded once she arrived. "This exchange really helps us understand one another," Sablan said. She hopes to visit Chinese museums to learn history beyond textbooks. Shared passions quickly bridged cultural gaps for some participants. Mo Jiaxin, a student at Renmin University of China, recalled how a casual mention of the Los Angeles Lakers sparked an energetic conversation with visiting Californian students. "When we open our hearts and engage with sincerity, understanding and resonance come naturally," Mo said. Kimball Schuenman, a middle school student from Utah, a western U.S. state, identified deeper common ground. Young people on both sides of the Pacific pursue quality education and fulfilling careers, while confronting shared global challenges: climate change and rapid AI-driven transformation. He views differing perspectives not as barriers, but as assets for solving those problems. "We come from different countries with different trains of thought. If we come together, we'll be able to think of different solutions," Schuenman said. The program also hosted structured, in-depth dialogue. At Tsinghua University, participants held three roundtable sessions on "Technology for Good: Innovation and Responsibility," debating how innovation can better serve human needs. Cao Ruoqi, a Tsinghua student, moderated a discussion on AI's evolving role in education and responsible AI use in classrooms. "Such discussions enable young people from diverse cultural backgrounds and life experiences to inspire one another and gain insights hard to acquire from reading alone," Cao said. She noted one panel cannot resolve complex global problems overnight, yet exchanges like this can "sow a seed in the lives of young people from both countries" that might "grow into a forest of lasting friendship and future cooperation." The Beijing gathering marks the latest step to revitalize China-U.S. youth exchanges. Wei Wei, a U.S. delegation team leader and Chinese teacher based in the United States, said American student demand for China travel continues to rise. "I feel a sense of responsibility to promote greater youth exchanges between the two countries, and help more students become cultural ambassadors," Wei said. ■

item.title: China urges automakers to resist irrational competition, ensure product safety
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
BEIJING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- Four Chinese government departments have urged major automakers to resist irrational competition, strengthen management of innovative vehicle designs and research and development (R&D) testing and validation, and ensure product safety, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) said Friday. The call came at a meeting Thursday with representatives from more than 30 major automakers, organized by relevant offices under the MIIT, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, and the State Administration for Market Regulation. Officials outlined requirements in a draft circular on strengthening the management of innovative vehicle designs and R&D testing and validation, and reported on problems identified during previous supervisory inspections. The meeting urged automakers to fulfill their primary responsibility for product safety, strengthen compliance, and conduct thorough safety assessments and R&D testing and validation to eliminate potential safety risks. It also called for truthful and objective marketing, warning against false, exaggerated or misleading claims, promotional activities depicting traffic violations, or messages encouraging drivers to neglect their responsibility for safe driving. Automakers were also asked to strengthen safety safeguards for intelligent connected new energy vehicles, improve safety assessment and testing management systems, strengthen production conformity assurance systems, and tighten supply chain oversight. Relevant authorities of the four departments will strengthen coordination, advance a special campaign to improve product quality, release and implement the circular as soon as possible, and accelerate the formulation and revision of relevant standards. They will also continue inspections of major automakers, deal firmly with companies found to have problems in accordance with laws and regulations, and make their cases public, according to the MIIT. ■

item.title: Chinese toy, gift makers eye new growth from reciprocal China-U.S. tariff cuts
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
*At their eighth round of economic and trade consultations from Sept. 20 to 23, China and the United States agreed on product lists for the 30-billion-U.S.-dollar reciprocal tariff reductions. The United States will reduce tariffs on Chinese imports including toys, home appliances, baby products, kitchen and bathroom goods, and holiday gifts. *Across China's manufacturing and trading hubs, exporters are already reporting stronger demand from U.S. customers. *For businesses that weathered last year's tariff hikes, a pickup in U.S. demand is welcome, but it is only part of the story. From seeking customers in new markets to refreshing the appeal of traditional products, Chinese exporters are finding ways to navigate trade uncertainty. HANGZHOU/GUANGZHOU, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Christmas is still over two months away, but Gong Yongqiang is already preparing for next year. Shuttling between the shop, factory and warehouse, the Yiwu merchant is checking raw-material stocks and developing new festive decorations. His shop in the "world's supermarket" Yiwu, east China's Zhejiang Province, is lined with Santa Claus figurines in various styles and sizes, the kind that will sit on mantels across the United States by December. A recent China-U.S. tariff agreement has given him fresh reason to look ahead with confidence. At their eighth round of economic and trade consultations from Sept. 20 to 23, China and the United States agreed on product lists for the 30-billion-U.S.-dollar reciprocal tariff reductions. The United States will reduce tariffs on Chinese imports including toys, home appliances, baby products, kitchen and bathroom goods, and holiday gifts. "I followed the consensus the moment it was announced," Gong said. "It is undoubtedly a positive signal for foreign trade on both sides." Harley Seyedin, chairman and president of the American Chamber of Commerce in South China, said the consensus sends a strong signal to markets and investors, helping businesses gain confidence to invest, expand and create jobs on both sides of the Pacific. "Certainty is the lifeblood of business," Seyedin said. Luo Zhiheng, chief economist at Yuekai Securities, said the tariff reductions signal that trade relations are easing, although their effect on the overall U.S. tariff burden on Chinese goods remains limited. Their significance, rather, lies in creating room for lower tariffs on some non-sensitive products and indicating the direction of future policy. U.S. ORDERS PICK UP Across China's manufacturing and trading hubs, exporters are already reporting stronger demand from U.S. customers. At her 15-square-meter store in the Yiwu International Trade Market, Nie Ziqin has packed the walls with Halloween decorations ranging from glowing spiders and pumpkin lanterns to horror masks, offering almost everything an American household needs for Halloween. "This is this year's bestseller. One client ordered hundreds of thousands," she said, holding up a light-up spider. Her factory is working overtime to fill cross-border e-commerce orders, sending goods to U.S. warehouses. "Many American clients are optimistic about China-U.S. economic and trade cooperation," Nie said. "Mutual benefit and win-win results are what everyone wants." The growth in her orders is expected to continue, building on a trend that emerged even before the September talks. Her U.S. export orders rose 20 percent year on year in the first eight months of 2026, with American buyers placing orders earlier than usual. As the world's largest Christmas goods hub, Yiwu supplies nearly 80 percent of the global market and ships more than 20,000 varieties to 178 countries and regions each year. The United States remains an important market for the city. The city's exports to the United States reached 104.51 billion yuan (about 15.55 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, surging 25.1 percent from the previous year. Further south, toy and gift manufacturers in Chenghai District, known as China's "toy capital," in the city of Shantou, south China's Guangdong Province, are seeing changes in both orders and price negotiations. Less than 400 square km in size, Chenghai nonetheless accounts for more than half of China's plastic toy output and about one-third of global production. "When tariffs go down, buyers' costs fall, which leaves more room for both sides. Price negotiation has become less difficult," said Guo Bo, general manager of Guangdong YiYu Craft & Hardware Electrical Factory Co., Ltd., a supplier of plush Santas, snowmen and reindeer. Guo expects order volume to increase 10 to 20 percent this year. Qiu Zhihong, chairman of Shantou Dave Plastic Toys Co., Ltd., also reported a recent improvement. His company manufactures licensed products for Disney and Universal Studios, with exports to the United States accounting for 30 to 40 percent of its exports. One U.S. customer who previously ordered 100 containers is now ordering 120, Qiu said. DIVERSIFYING MARKETS, INNOVATING PRODUCTS For businesses that weathered last year's tariff hikes, a pickup in U.S. demand is welcome, but it is only part of the story. From seeking customers in new markets to refreshing the appeal of traditional products, Chinese exporters are finding ways to navigate trade uncertainty. In Yiwu, Gong Yongqiang has learned not to rely too heavily on any single market. After the tariff increases, the U.S. share of his sales fell from a peak of about a quarter to around 10 percent. But orders from Brazil, Colombia and Chile helped fill the gap, expanding his customer base to more than 30 countries and regions. He is also designing new products. This year, Gong has launched more than 100 new designs, adding sound and movement to traditional static Christmas figurines. Such features typically boost profit margins by more than 10 percent, he said. Now, he is developing an AI-powered Christmas doll that can hold conversations, with a launch planned for next year. In Chenghai, Qiu Zhihong is taking a similar approach. Touch-sensitive AI toys are outselling basic models, he said, prompting his company to invest in smarter products and stronger brands. It is also working directly with retailers to cut out intermediaries. For Chinese exporters, these efforts to diversify markets and innovate products are already opening doors. Earlier this month, Yiwu merchant Tao Yang secured an order from an American customer for more than 2,000 embroidered denim jackets. The order was modest in value, but it showed how fresh designs and tailored products can help Chinese exporters win over overseas customers and build long-term business relationships. "When the client came to Yiwu in September, we used AI-assisted design and fine-tuned every detail with him in person. That's how we met his needs and closed the deal," Tao said. Tao noted that this agility is powered by Yiwu's robust supply and industrial chains, along with a keen understanding of the market, enabling rapid product design and scaled-up production. Luo Zhiheng, the economist, said Chinese exporters' resilience in the future will depend on diversifying markets, upgrading technology, building stronger brands and expanding their international presence. ■

item.title: One month to go: APEC CEO Summit 2026 to help promote cooperation, prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
BEIJING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- The APEC CEO Summit 2026 will be held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 17 and 18, with one month to go before the region's top business and government leaders gather to chart a course for Asia-Pacific prosperity. Under the theme "promoting prosperity together for a win-win future," several APEC economy leaders will attend alongside business representatives, with discussions covering Asia-Pacific free trade area development, connectivity, artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and sustainable development. The two-day event is organized by the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT). Ng Yih Pyng, president of the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia, said he looks forward to this summit driving smoother trade and economic flows, deeper industrial cooperation and more tangible business opportunities for companies across the region. He called for progress on trade facilitation, lower cross-border business costs, and more cooperation in digital trade, AI applications, talent training and green technology. An important event in the APEC calendar, the APEC CEO Summit has been held annually since 1996, serving as the highest-level platform for APEC economy leaders and business representatives to discuss open cooperation and advance regional economic development. China has identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priority areas for this year's APEC cooperation, responding to the new opportunities and challenges facing the region. Business leaders believe the three priorities reflect the broadest common ground among all parties. Masaharu Nakayama, executive officer of Panasonic Holdings Corporation Group, said Asia Pacific's economic dynamism is rooted in open cooperation. The business community should deepen supply chain and value chain integration, tap new opportunities in AI, the digital economy and sustainable development through stronger connectivity, and together expand the pie of cooperation so that development benefits all economies in the region, he said. On innovation cooperation, Ng highlighted the complementarity between Malaysia and China. China has rich experience in digital technology, AI, advanced manufacturing and e-commerce, while Malaysia offers a solid manufacturing base, diverse talent and ASEAN business networks, he said, noting that the two countries could move toward industrial and innovation partners to explore regional markets. During the 2026 APEC "China Year," regional business cooperation has advanced steadily, with deeper consensus on strengthening cooperation, tighter connectivity, and a stronger foundation for practical collaboration. Ren Hongbin, chairman of the CCPIT, said the CCPIT will host a high-quality summit and launch a Shenzhen initiative to facilitate the building of the Asia-Pacific community. ■

item.title: Xiplomacy: Xi's decades-long commitment to poverty reduction
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
BEIJING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- Poverty eradication is "a common ideal of humanity," Chinese President Xi Jinping has once said. Five years after China declared a complete victory in the fight against absolute poverty in 2021, its approach continues to inspire poverty reduction efforts worldwide. Xi's dedication to poverty alleviation spans decades, from his early work in poor rural communities to the nationwide campaign he led and his efforts to promote international cooperation -- a long-running endeavor that resonates as the world marks the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty on Saturday. A DECADES-LONG PURSUIT "A weak hatchling bird can be the first to fly, and the poorest can be the first to become rich," Xi wrote in a 1988 essay on the development of Ningde Prefecture in east China's Fujian Province. The following summer, Xi, then Ningde's Party secretary, traveled by car and on foot to reach Xiadang, a remote mountain township that had no road access. Xi returned to Xiadang twice, helping tackle problems with roads, electricity and water supplies. In 2019, residents wrote to tell him that their township had shaken off poverty, and he replied with congratulations. After becoming China's top leader, Xi continued his hands-on approach to poverty reduction. He conducted more than 50 inspections and research visits related to poverty alleviation, traveling to all 14 of the country's contiguous areas of extreme poverty. In February 2018, Xi visited impoverished Yi families in Zhaojue County, Sichuan Province, asking about their livelihoods and discussing ways to tackle poverty with villagers and local officials. "Not a single ethnic group or family should be left behind in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects," he said during the visit. On Feb. 25, 2021, Xi declared a "complete victory" in China's fight against absolute poverty. Over eight years, nearly 100 million rural residents had been lifted out of absolute poverty, enabling the country to meet the poverty reduction target of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development a decade ahead of schedule. In a congratulatory letter to Xi, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the achievement "a reason for hope and inspiration to the entire community of nations." LESSONS BEYOND BORDERS China's poverty reduction experience has attracted attention from leaders around the world, some of whom have sought inspiration from Xi's writings and visited places where his ideas were put into practice. Xi's early ideas on poverty reduction and economic development were collected in "Up and Out of Poverty," a collection of speeches, articles and interviews from 1988 to 1990 during his tenure in Ningde. Explaining the title, Xi wrote that its significance lay first and foremost in uprooting the "poverty mentality" and "poverty thinking." In a foreword to the book's Uzbek edition published in 2023, President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev said the work remained an important source of guidance for state and social governance more than three decades after its initial publication. During his visit to China this month, President of Botswana Duma Gideon Boko traveled to Fuzhou and Ningde in Fujian Province, where Xi once worked, and visited an exhibition on poverty reduction. During talks with Xi in Beijing, Boko depicted China's development as "an economic and political miracle never seen in history." In June 2018, Bounnhang Vorachith, then President of Laos, visited Shibadong Village in central China's Hunan Province to learn about China's approach to poverty reduction. In villager Shi Basan's home, he paused before a photograph showing Xi chatting with her beside a fire pit. During that November 2013 visit, Xi first proposed "targeted poverty alleviation" in a discussion with villagers, calling for measures tailored to local conditions and each household's needs. After retracing Xi's route and speaking with residents, Bounnhang voiced hope of bringing the village's experience back to Laos. In reply to a letter from the villagers the following year, he praised Shibadong's success as offering invaluable lessons for his country. In September 2026, Prime Minister of Madagascar Mamitiana Rajaonarison also visited Shibadong, where he witnessed first-hand residents' changing lives and watched demonstrations of traditional Miao ethnic embroidery. He said the visit shown him Xi's deep concern for the people and provided inspiration for Madagascar. TURNING EXPERIENCE INTO ACTION Xi's efforts to share China's poverty reduction experience abroad date back to his early tenure in Fujian Province. There, he promoted Juncao technology as part of Fujian's poverty reduction cooperation with northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. In 2000, he introduced the technology to a visiting governor from Papua New Guinea and later helped establish a China-aided Juncao demonstration base in the Pacific island country. Juncao technology uses grass to cultivate mushrooms and provide livestock feed. The technology has spread to more than 100 countries, creating hundreds of thousands of jobs. In Zimbabwe, farmer Mandiudza Masvongo has earned 330 U.S. dollars from selling mushrooms since taking up Juncao cultivation in June 2025. The proceeds have helped her start a small cleaning products business, which she said could mark a turning point in her life. Beyond agriculture, China's development assistance has also improved basic services and created opportunities for small businesses. In Cambodia's Tanorn village, a China-aided project brought better roads, clean water and solar power. Por Sokhim, once dependent on rice farming, now runs a grocery store, while her husband operates a motorcycle repair shop. In 2021, Xi proposed the Global Development Initiative, with poverty reduction and food security among its priorities. In the five years since its launch, cooperation projects under the initiative have taken root and delivered tangible results in more than 120 countries. At the 2024 G20 summit in Rio de Janeiro, Xi drew upon China's experience to express confidence in the prospects for poverty reduction across the developing world. "If China can make it, other developing countries can make it too. This is what China's battle against poverty says to the world," he told world leaders. ■

item.title: China's storage deployment helping change economics of renewable electricity: IRENA official
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
FUZHOU, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 World Energy Storage Conference runs from Wednesday to Friday in Ningde City, east China's Fujian Province, bringing together participants to discuss cutting-edge technologies, prospects for the energy storage industry, and China's position in the global energy storage market. In 2025, global annual battery storage additions hit roughly 307 GWh, with China accounting for 56 percent. The scale of deployment in China has become central to the global storage market and is "helping to change the economics of renewable electricity," said Ilina Stefanova, head of the Coalition for Action at the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), at the opening ceremony. China's experience in technology, manufacturing, deployment and grid integration will matter not only domestically, but also for the global energy transition, she added. As renewables become a major energy source worldwide, storage is evolving from a supporting facility into essential new infrastructure for power systems. It must meet diverse grid demands while continuously improving reliability and stability, said Zeng Yuqun, founder and chairman of China's leading battery manufacturer CATL, which is based in Ningde City. Industry figures show China is responding to these demands. China's new-type storage industry has achieved notable results, said Xiong Jijun, vice minister of industry and information technology, in the opening speech. China's storage battery output exceeded 420 GWh in the first half of 2026, up about 110 percent year on year. The industry is advancing along multiple technological routes, with lithium batteries playing a leading role alongside sodium-ion and flow batteries. The government will balance development and safety, strengthen technological innovation, adhere to demand-driven principles and foster a global industrial ecosystem, while firmly guarding against rat race competition and guiding the industry from scale expansion toward innovation-led growth, Xiong added. Ningde City has hosted the conference three times previously, an event that has attracted representatives from governments, industries and academia in over 50 countries and regions. ■

item.title: Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, visits the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve in Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, Oct. 16, 2026. Xi made an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) ULANQAB, Inner Mongolia, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded. During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area. He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner. Xi visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry. Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule. He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces. Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, talks with staff members while visiting Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, Oct. 16, 2026.
